newsitem.title: POLAND: Creditanstalt Polish unit sues Universal.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt Polish unit sues Universal.

text.p: Creditanstalt Securities SA is suing Polish trader Universal SA and financial daily Parkiet for making allegedly false accusations against it in a newspaper interview, Creditanstalt said in a statement.
Creditanstalt Securities SA is the Polish unit of the Creditanstalt Investment Banking Group.

"Creditanstalt Securitities opened up litigation procedures in the Warsaw District Court on January 20, 1997. The only purpose of the court case is to protect Creditanstalt's reputation," the statement said.
Universal spokeswoman Agnieszka Szostek said the firm had no comment until it received an official court summons.
Creditanstalt said it was contesting Universal President Dariusz Przywieczerski's comments made in an interview published on December 7, 1996.

"In the interview Mr Przywieczerski stated that Creditanstalt Securities SA did not forecast correctly Universal's annual net profit, analysed Universal in the view of underwriting its (1994) share offer and later refused to do it," Creditanstalt said.
"(He stated that Creditanstalt) used insider information to buy its shares at a lower price and later re-sold them with a broad profit. The accusations are all false," it added.

"We never considered to underwrite shares, we analysed Universal's situation because Universal wanted a loan secured by their shares," Anna Wolek, Creditanstalt Securities SA Corporate Communications Manager, told Reuters on Monday.
She said Universal did not receive the loan.

Wolek said Creditanstalt's 1996 12.3-million-zloty net profit forecast for Universal, which fell short of the trader's nine-month result of 15.4 million, was made before it knew Universal had won 15 million zlotys in tax refunds.
Universal won the refunds in July and August last year.

The statement said Creditanstalt amended its profit forecast to 20 million zlotys in its Monthly Market Review published on December 2 and did not acquire shares in Universal's 1994 secondary offering.
Wolek said Creditanstalt did not want to make any profit in the case and that its financial demand of 30,000 zlotys would be for the benefit of the Polish Red Cross.
